skills.name: Use the laws of logarithms and solve logarithmic and exponential equations

note.text:
log_b x = y means bʸ = x. So log_2 8 = 3 because 2³ = 8.
Laws: log(xy) = log x + log y; log(x/y) = log x − log y; log xⁿ = n log x; log_b b = 1; log_b 1 = 0.
Logarithmic equations: rewrite as a power. log_3(x + 1) = 2 → x + 1 = 3² → x = 8.
Exponential equations with unmatched bases: take logs. 2ˣ = 7 → x log 2 = log 7 → x = log 7 ÷ log 2 ≈ 2.81.
Note: log x + log y is NOT log(x + y).

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text:
By the end, you should be able to use the laws of logarithms, solve log equations by rewriting them as powers, and solve bˣ = n by taking logs.
Builds on: Form Three logarithms and Lesson {27} (exponential equations).
Leads to: growth and decay problems (interest, populations) and Form Five logarithmic functions.

sections.heading: Laws, revised
sections.text:
log_b x = y means b{sup('y')} = x. For example log₂ {8} = {3} and log₁₀ {1000} = {3}.
• log x + log y = log(xy)  • log x − log y = log(x/y)  • log xⁿ = n log x
• log_b b = {1} and log_b {1} = {0}.
Example: log₆ {4} + log₆ {9} = log₆ {36} = {2}.
Warning: log x + log y is not log(x + y), and log x ÷ log y is not log(x − y).

sections.heading: Solving
sections.text:
• A log equation: rewrite as a power. log₃(x + {1}) = {2} → x + {1} = {3}{sup(2)} = {9} → x = {8}.
• Combine logs first: log₂ x + log₂ {4} = {5} → log₂ {4}x = {5} → {4}x = {32} → x = {8}.
• An exponential equation whose sides are not powers of the same base: take logs.
{2}ˣ = {7} → x log {2} = log {7} → x = {roundTo(log10(7), 0.0001)} ÷ {roundTo(log10(2), 0.0001)} ≈ {roundTo(log10(7) / log10(2), 0.01)}.
Check: {2}{sup(2)} = {4} < {7} < {8} = {2}{sup(3)}, so x is between {2} and {3}.

key_words.meaning: the index: log_b x is the power of b that gives x
b in log_b x; log means log₁₀ on a calculator
apply log to both sides of an equation

mistake.why: Adding logs multiplies the numbers inside: {2} × {3} = {6}.

worked_example.problem: Solve {b}ˣ = {n}, giving x to {2} decimal places.
steps: {n} is not a power of {b}, so take logs of both sides: log({b}ˣ) = log {n}.

cards.idea: log_b x asks: b to what power gives x?
Adding logs multiplies the numbers inside; subtracting divides them.
Take logs to bring an unknown index down: log(bˣ) = x log b.

misconceptions.explain: Divide the logs, not the numbers: log {n} ÷ log {b}.
x log {b} = log {n}: divide by log {b}; log {n} − log {b} is log({n}/{b}).
The log is the index, not {b ^ k} ÷ {b}.

solution: log{sub(b)} {b ^ k} asks: {b} to what power gives {b ^ k}?
Rewrite as a power: x + {d} = {b}{sup(k)} = {b ^ k}.

misconceptions.explain: log x + log {c} = log({c}x): divide by {c}, do not subtract.
Rewrite the whole equation first: {c}x = {b ^ k}.
